title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in South Sudan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in South Sudan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for South Sudan: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Preparing medical records, legal representation, civil identity files, and disability benefits during a serious illness in South Sudan requires careful advance planning. Institutional fragility and the absence of comprehensive public online civil-registry or statutory gazette portals limit remote verification of domestic .gov.ss websites (several judicial and ministry domains are offline or fail security certificate checks). Accordingly, this guide relies on live agency and diplomatic mission pages alongside verified international legal archives (FAOLEX, ILO NATLEX, WIPO Lex, Refworld, and HCCH) and foreign consular reciprocity notices, and you should verify active filing steps locally or through an embassy.

steps.title: Gather clinical summaries and evaluate specialist care or evacuation options
steps.html:
• Request signed medical histories, diagnostic imaging, laboratory results, and physician fitness-to-travel assessments directly from Juba Teaching Hospital or the treating clinic.
  • Review private medical insurance and emergency evacuation options early, because tertiary oncology, specialized palliative infrastructure, and specialist diagnostic capacity outside Juba are severely constrained.
  • Clarify preferred healthcare decision-makers in writing with attending physicians and family, noting that South Sudan lacks a statutory public advance-directive registry and official administrative procedures rely on formal civil and marital documentation verified locally [14].

steps.title: Execute a formal Power of Attorney for local representation
steps.html:
• Grant clear written authority to a trusted family member or local advocate to manage bank accounts, land committees, salary claims, and government filings, because South Sudanese offices rely overwhelmingly on in-person attendance.
  • Inside South Sudan, execute the mandate before an advocate or Commissioner for Oaths; outside the country, request consular execution through an accredited South Sudanese mission such as the Embassy of the Republic of South Sudan in London, which requires a written request from the applicant, a copy of their passport or ID, and two witnesses presenting valid photo identification [7].

steps.title: Verify civil identity documents and court or customary jurisdiction
steps.html:
• Confirm that Nationality Certificates, passports, and civil status records are current and consistent with rules administered by the Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passports and Immigration (DNPI) under the Nationality Act 2011 and the 2024 civil registration decrees [1][10][11].
  • Understand the dual judicial framework when organizing property, family guardianship, or business authority: statutory jurisdiction sits with State High Courts and County Courts under Part Seven of the Transitional Constitution 2011 and the Judiciary Act 2008 [5], whereas community land administration and local disputes frequently involve local councils and Customary Law Courts established under the Local Government Act 2009 [4].

steps.title: Review sick-leave, work-injury, and disability pension protections
steps.html:
• Examine statutory sick leave, medical termination safeguards, and employment injury benefits under the Labour Act (No. 64), 2017 (available via Refworld and FAOLEX) [2][12].
  • For civil servants and public employees, check medical-retirement, invalidity pension, and lump-sum benefit rules with the Ministry of Finance and Planning under the Civil Service Pensions Scheme Act 2013 and the Pension Funds Act 2012 [3][6].

steps.title: Draft a written will and complete non-Apostille consular authentication
steps.html:
• Prepare a clear written will with a South Sudanese legal practitioner addressing property held under both statutory titles and customary land allocations, ensuring it aligns with High Court requirements and probate recognition standards referenced in statutory law [5][13].
  • Complete international document authentication carefully because South Sudan is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [9].
  • Domestic documents destined abroad require authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation in Juba followed by receiving embassy legalization, while foreign medical or Power of Attorney records intended for South Sudan require home-country Foreign Ministry certification (such as the UK FCDO or U.S. Department of State) followed by authentication at a South Sudanese mission such as the Embassy of the Republic of South Sudan in London (cash fees GBP 20 for civil/immigration documents, GBP 50 for commercial documents) [8][14].

contacts.name: Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passports and Immigration
contacts.note: Ministry of Interior directorate responsible for South Sudanese civil registry, nationality certificates, and passport administration.

contacts.name: Embassy of the Republic of South Sudan in London
contacts.note: Processes consular Powers of Attorney (requires two ID-holding witnesses) and document authentication (Office 11, 21 Knightsbridge, London).

contacts.name: Ministry of Finance and Planning
contacts.note: Publishes the Civil Service Pensions Scheme Act 2013 governing public-sector invalidity and retirement pensions.
